Extend a short gauge record of window statistics from donor gauges

Source: R/wet_window_extend.R
wet_window_extend.Rd

Extends a target gauge's per-year window statistics (from wet_window_stats()) into the years it has no record, from nearby gauges that have one, with a prediction interval per year. The donors are the k gauges nearest the target in predictor space (easting and northing in km in BC Albers, EPSG:3005, and log drainage area, each divided by its standard deviation over stations) that have a value in every year the target has. In each year to be extended, the nearest of them with a value that year supplies it; each donor's relation to the target is fitted on the target's years. A year none of them has is not returned.

Usage

wet_window_extend(
  x,
  stations,
  target,
  method = c("ols", "move1", "ratio"),
  k = 5,
  level = 0.9,
  resid = NULL
)

Arguments

x

Window statistics in wet_window_stats()'s long format (station_number, variable, period, year, value) for the target and its candidate donors. Each variable and period is extended on its own. The target's rows are its record: to hold years out, leave them out.

stations

data.frame(station_number, lon, lat, drainage_area_gross_km2), as from wet_station_select(), with a row for the target and every station in x. The predictor scaling is taken over its rows.

target

The target's station number.

method

"ols", "move1" or "ratio".

k

Number of nearest covering donors in the chain.

level

Nominal coverage of the interval.

resid

For "move1" and "ratio": residuals whose (1 - level) / 2 and (1 + level) / 2 quantiles bound the interval.

Value

A data frame: station_number (the target), variable, period, year, value, lower, upper, donor (NA for an observed year) and source ("observed" or "extended"), ordered by variable, period and year. Attribute "donors": the chain per variable and period, nearest first.

Details

A statistic named *_cov_day (a day of the window) is related in days; every other statistic in logs, and a value of 0 or less is left out of the fit (counted in the attribute "dropped").

Methods

With x the donor's value and y the target's (log or days) over the target's n years:

"ols"

Least-squares regression of y on x. The interval is the regression's prediction interval at level, with n - 2 degrees of freedom.

"move1"

The line of organic correlation (MOVE.1), y = mean(y) + sign(r) sd(y) / sd(x) (x - mean(x)), which keeps the target's variance where regression shrinks it.

"ratio"

The donor's value times the ratio of the target's mean to the donor's mean over the same years, on the original scale.

For "move1" and "ratio" the interval comes from resid: residuals (observed minus predicted, on the method's scale) measured elsewhere, for example at other gauges held out; without them the bounds are NA. A log-scale prediction is returned back-transformed, so it is a median.

Examples

# Three gauges: a long-record donor, a farther one, and a target with five
# years whose flow is 0.4 times the donor's to the power 1.1
set.seed(1)
yrs <- 1961:2020
d1 <- exp(rnorm(60, 3, 0.3))
d2 <- exp(rnorm(60, 3, 0.3))
x <- data.frame(
  station_number = rep(c("D1", "D2", "T"), c(60, 60, 5)),
  variable = "q_mean", period = "migration",
  year = c(yrs, yrs, 1975:1979),
  value = c(d1, d2, 0.4 * d1[15:19]^1.1 * exp(rnorm(5, 0, 0.05))))
st <- data.frame(station_number = c("D1", "D2", "T"), lon = c(-126.6, -127.8, -126.5),
                 lat = c(54.4, 55.1, 54.3), drainage_area_gross_km2 = c(2300, 900, 360))
e <- wet_window_extend(x, st, "T", method = "ols")
head(e)
#>   station_number variable    period year     value     lower     upper donor
#> 1              T   q_mean migration 1961  9.320742  8.318057 10.444294    D1
#> 2              T   q_mean migration 1962 11.755876 10.795855 12.801267    D1
#> 3              T   q_mean migration 1963  8.778530  7.754761  9.937456    D1
#> 4              T   q_mean migration 1964 17.616199 15.836770 19.595567    D1
#> 5              T   q_mean migration 1965 12.257606 11.283639 13.315642    D1
#> 6              T   q_mean migration 1966  8.816745  7.794467  9.973099    D1
#>     source
#> 1 extended
#> 2 extended
#> 3 extended
#> 4 extended
#> 5 extended
#> 6 extended
table(e$source, e$donor, useNA = "ifany")
#>           
#>            D1 <NA>
#>   extended 55    0
#>   observed  0    5
